channel.title: Read James Wolfe
channel.description: Helping weary Christians find comfort and confidence in Christ.

item.title: On the Patience of God
item.description: There is a particular kind of shame that visits us not when we fail, but when we fail again — the same sin, the same excuse, the same quiet apology whispered for the hundredth time. I used to think God's patience had a bottom. I am learning, slowly, that it does not.

item.title: The Ordinary Tuesday
item.description: Most of my sanctification has not happened on mountaintops. It has happened in the dishes, in the traffic, in the eleventh phone call from a friend in crisis when I had nothing left to give. I am starting to suspect that this — the unremarkable middle of the week — is where most of the Christian life actually takes place.

item.title: What the Psalms Taught Me About Complaint
item.description: For years I thought lament was a failure of faith — a crack in the foundation that a stronger Christian wouldn't need. Then I read the Psalms honestly for the first time and realized how much of Israel's worship was, quite plainly, complaint addressed to God rather than about him.

item.title: A Slower Kind of Faithfulness
item.description: We have built a culture that rewards the dramatic testimony and quietly ignores the fifty-year marriage, the unremarkable deacon, the Sunday school teacher nobody wrote a book about. I want to make a case for the long, undramatic obedience that most of us are actually called to.
